about.title: Rosemead Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Rosemead sees steady traffic pressure where Walnut Grove Avenue, Garvey Avenue, and Valley Boulevard feed into the I-10, and public records show 216 injury collisions and 275 injured people in the most recent final year, with Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. a common time for reported crashes. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the days right after matter — insurers move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness contact information can disappear quickly. We handle personal injury claims for Rosemead residents injured in car accidents. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Before you talk to an insurance adjuster or agree to a recorded statement, it helps to have our team in your corner — we understand how Los Angeles County claims are handled and how comparative fault can affect your case.

items.title: California's Fault Rules Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: Under pure comparative fault, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — the amount is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You May Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering Claims
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in car accident cases, which is why documenting your recovery matters from day one.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid recorded statements until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to minimize what they owe, and details can be twisted even when you're being honest. Our team can advise you on what to say and what to hold back.

items.question: What if my crash happened at a Rosemead intersection with a lot of reported collisions, like along Garvey Avenue?
items.answer: Public collision counts on corridors like Garvey Avenue, Valley Boulevard, and the I-10 through Rosemead simply reflect traffic volume and reporting, not a legal judgment about the road itself. What matters for your claim is the specific facts of your crash — who did what, and what evidence exists. We can help gather that evidence while it's still fresh.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit in California. If a government entity, like a city vehicle or a poorly maintained public road, played a role, that deadline can be as short as six months, so acting quickly matters.
